policy: This is a per-alert review record, not an automatic suppression list. A prior rule/path match never authorizes dismissal without checking the current source, sink and caller boundaries. Compatibility behavior is preserved; genuine issues are fixed. GitHub dispositions require explicit evidence and do not disable queries.
context: The formatting migration reopened 50 previously triaged rule/path pairs. All 62 current alerts were independently reviewed; fixes are kept separate from intentional-flow decisions.

reviewedNewSink.evidence: The intended public archive-to-cache flow has no credentials. Callers pin URLs and SHA-256; the helper enforces a 60-second deadline and 64 MiB cap, compares the digest before persisting, and atomically publishes an exclusive temporary file. Consumers rehash before extraction/execution. Any remaining analyzer result at this sink requires an exact current-flow review, not a blanket rule exclusion.

entries.evidence: Individually reviewed this new source, sink and caller rather than inheriting an earlier rule/path decision. The fixture obtains runtime.active.get(its own loopback origin); startAgentServer binds literal 127.0.0.1 on an owned ephemeral port, generates the credential and exclusively writes its 0600 discovery file before returning the same in-memory endpoint. The test now uses production readDiscovery (bounded 64 KiB descriptor read, schema/token validation, exact HTTP 127.0.0.1 endpoint with explicit port and no userinfo/path/query/hash), asserts the parsed endpoint equals that in-memory owned endpoint, and sends the credential only as Authorization to /v1/session. Redirects are refused, the request has a five-second bound, HTTP 200 remains asserted, and the response body is always canceled.
